correctness.rationale: For arbitrary p, q=p^e and g of degree m with d=pm>q, the affine part is smooth since the x-derivative is -1; only P=[0:1:0] lies at infinity. In local chart Y=1, char-p differentiation gives f_x=-z^(d-1), f_z=-(d-1)xz^(d-2), reducing the Tjurina algebra to R/(z^(d-2)(x,z)), R=k[[x,z]]/(h). Since h(x,0)=-a_m x^d !=0, z is R-regular, and the exact sequence contributes length 1 plus (d-2)d, proving (d-1)^2. Independent finite Groebner computations in characteristics 2,3,5 and nonmonomial g agree; they are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete Tjurina singular-scheme length is a natural deformation-sensitive invariant of the entire Artin--Schreier family of plane curves with one wild cusp. Its unexpectedly uniform value (d-1)^2 is independent of the chosen prime-power parameter and all lower coefficients, despite changing singularity geometry; this supplies useful scheme-theoretic information not contained in the reduced cusp count or the stated multiplicity. It applies to arbitrarily large degree and all primes rather than one isolated computation.
